The Problem We're Hiring You to Solve
Most architects know systems. A few know mortgage. Almost none understand it from both sides of the table: the lender and servicer technology that originates and manages loans, and the federal agency that guarantees those loans and holds industry accountable.
We are hiring one of the few. You will own the enterprise and solution architecture for the modernization of a federal home loan benefit program, translating statute, policy, and two decades of accumulated business rules into a modern platform while the 20-year-old legacy system keeps running underneath it. If you can hold the loan lifecycle and the oversight lens in your head at the same time, keep reading.
The Opportunity
This program is replacing the technology behind a nationwide home loan guaranty operation. That means origination-adjacent workflows, servicing oversight, loss mitigation, claims, grants, analytics, and the data exchanges that connect a federal agency to thousands of external lender and servicer users.

The target platform is Salesforce-centered, supplemented by serverless capabilities in a government cloud. The legacy platform stays alive, integrated, and secure until the modern one absorbs its functions and the bridges between them come down.
Your job sits at the point where all of it must cohere. Requirements arrive as business needs, policy decisions, and process flows. Development teams need buildable designs with traceability, data models, integration specifications, and test strategies.

The customer needs an architect who can explain why a design decision protects the program, not just how it works. And the whole effort runs on a fast clock: intake requests turn into executable plans in days, releases ship monthly, and architecture decisions that stall become delivery risks with your name on them.
This is not an ivory-tower architecture role. Your designs get built, deployed, and measured within weeks of leaving your hands, and you stay accountable for whether they hold up in production.
Why the domain requirement is real. Plenty of strong architects can design an integration. Very few can look at a servicing data exchange and know which fields carry regulatory weight, why the agency needs lineage on a particular data element, or where a workflow change quietly breaks a downstream claim calculation. This program moves too fast to teach you mortgage while you architect it. We need someone who walks in fluent.
What You'll Own
The target-state architecture. Define and defend one coherent enterprise architecture across the product line: legacy systems, the modern platform, and everything bridging them. Teams and the customer should make decisions against your picture of where the program is going, not their own private versions of it.
Solution designs that survive contact with development. Turn approved requirements into complete solution packages: architecture and state diagrams, data models, API and interface specifications, integration designs, and test strategies with full traceability back to the business need. The bar is that development builds from your package without re-litigating it.
The configure-versus-customize line. The program mandates out-of-the-box and configuration-first solutions, with custom code as an approved exception. You decide what is configured, what is customized, and why, and you defend those calls to the customer's change authority with evidence.
Data architecture and lineage. Own the logical and physical data models, data dictionaries, and the migration and bridging strategy that moves a 20-year accumulation of loan data into the modern platform without breaking the processes still running on the old one. Design data governance enforcement in, not around.
Industry-facing integration architecture. Design the APIs, batch exchanges, and system-to-system transfers that connect the agency to lenders, servicers, and partner systems. Fluency in mortgage data standards such as MISMO is part of the job. Resilience, self-recovery, and monitoring are design requirements, not operational afterthoughts.
The legacy decommissioning roadmap. Sequence which functions move when, design the bridge services that keep both platforms consistent during the transition, and plan the retirement of every bridge you create.
Fast, credible solution judgment. New needs enter through a formal intake process that produces an executable plan, with scope and level of effort, in days. Your architecture instincts have to be right at speed, and honest about uncertainty when they cannot be.
Security and compliance as design inputs. Zero Trust alignment, accessibility, data protection, and authorization evidence get engineered into your designs from the first diagram, because retrofitting them is how federal programs lose months.
The architecture bar for the program. Run design reviews, mentor engineers and analysts on architectural thinking, document the standards, and hold the line on them, including against pressure from delivery deadlines.
AI-Native Architecture
AI is part of how PhoenixTeam works, and this role has more to gain from it than most.
We are looking for someone who already uses tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot, or comparable AI tools, as a working part of their practice.

For an architect on this program, the leverage looks like: analyzing legacy code and data structures to recover business rules that exist nowhere else, accelerating the production of data models, interface specifications, and architecture documentation, pressure-testing designs against edge cases before development finds them, and prototyping integration patterns in hours instead of weeks.
You will also help decide where AI belongs inside the solutions themselves, and where it does not, given federal security, data, and authorization boundaries.
Two things anchor all of it. Judgment stays human: you know when AI output is wrong, incomplete, or inappropriate for a federal system of record, and you review accordingly. And boundaries are non-negotiable: federal environments govern what tools may touch government code, systems, and data. Use AI wherever it creates leverage, and understand the security, data, privacy, and authorization boundaries governing where and how it can be used.

About DuploCloud
DuploCloud is an Agentic Internal Developer Platform (IDP) for DevOps and platform engineering teams. With DuploCloud , teams can automate any complex DevOps use case as an AI agent and deploy it to their entire organization in a matter of hours to days, instead of the months it has traditionally taken.

Ephemeral environments, release management, deployment automation, Kubernetes upgrades, incident triage, security patching, compliance remediation, Terraform drift detection and remediation: each becomes a governed, multi-user agent that runs inside the customer's own cloud.
Our premise is the 70/30 problem: every DevOps workflow is bespoke, but roughly 70% of what it does is the same set of functions over and over (kubectl access, tailing logs, deploying a microservice, triggering pipelines, observability, compliance reports, cost dashboards, Terraform modules), while the remaining ~30% is the logic specific to that organization.

DuploCloud delivers the common core as a shared platform and lets teams build only their custom delta as Agents on top.

The product has two components: the Agent Platform, powered by ARMOR (Agent Runtime for Multiplayer Operations), which provides shared multiplayer AI sessions, workspaces, SSO and RBAC, secrets management, audit trails, human-in-the-loop approvals, token cost controls and a Model Router for per-workflow LLM choice across Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and open-source models; and the Coding Assistant, a Claude Code plugin paired with our DevKit that lets a platform engineer describe a use case in plain English, build and test the resulting Agent against a local copy of the platform on their laptop, and publish it to their organization.

Agents ship with rich UX (forms, wizards, dashboards, status views) and are invocable from the Web UI, API, CLI, MCP, Terraform provider, and Slack/Teams. Routine, high-frequency actions run token-less as pre-coded scripts, reserving the LLM for judgment.
The platform runs fully self-hosted in the customer's cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, onprem) or DuploCloud -managed, supports SOC 2, HIPAA and PCI compliance requirements, and is used by engineering organizations from high-growth startups to the enterprise. Headquartered in San Jose, DuploCloud is a venture backed company, Series-B funded by WestBridge Capital and StepStone Group.

About cogify group
cogify was founded in Switzerland in 2018 and today combines expertise in consulting, AI, software engineering, cybersecurity and digital products.
We are expanding our cybersecurity capabilities and are looking for a Cybersecurity Architect with a strong focus on Zero Trust who understands complex IT environments and can translate security requirements into practical, implementable solutions.

As a Cybersecurity Architect, you work at the interface between business, security, technology and delivery .
You understand the challenges our customers face, assess existing environments and identify where security needs to evolve.
You combine consulting skills with strong technical expertise – from the first assessment and target architecture through technology selection and implementation together with our engineering teams.
You ask the right questions, challenge existing assumptions and communicate confidently with stakeholders from management to engineering teams .

Assess existing IT and security environments and identify risks, gaps and improvement opportunities
Design Zero Trust and enterprise security target architectures
Develop practical security roadmaps and implementation concepts
Advise customers on security architecture, Zero Trust strategy and technology selection
Design solutions across IAM, ZTNA, SASE, network segmentation, cloud and endpoint security
Evaluate security technologies, products and licensing models against customer requirements
Translate business, security and compliance requirements into technically implementable solutions
Lead security workshops and architecture discussions with customers
Support implementation together with cybersecurity, cloud, infrastructure, DevOps and software engineers
Help shape and further develop cogify’s cybersecurity offering
Your Profile
Experience in cybersecurity architecture, security engineering, cybersecurity consulting or a comparable role
Strong understanding of Zero Trust architectures, technologies and principles
Good knowledge of frameworks such as NIST SP 800-207, CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model or comparable approaches
Strong knowledge of areas such as IAM, ZTNA, SASE, network security, segmentation, cloud security and access control
Experience designing or implementing enterprise security solutions
Ability to evaluate security technologies and select appropriate solutions for specific requirements
Strong understanding of enterprise networks, identity, authentication and cloud environments
Ability to translate complex security topics into clear decisions and practical solutions
Confident communication with both business and technical stakeholders
Independent, pragmatic and quality-focused way of working
Fluent English or German is required

Certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, SABSA, ISSAP or comparable qualifications
Experience with Microsoft Entra ID, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike or similar technologies
Experience with Azure, AWS or Google Cloud
Experience in regulated or security-sensitive environments
German, French or other languages in addition to your primary working language

At cogify, cybersecurity doesn’t end with an assessment or presentation.
You work directly with customers on real security challenges and stay involved when architecture becomes implementation.
The role combines cybersecurity consulting, architecture and technology , while giving you the opportunity to work closely with our engineering teams and actively shape a growing cybersecurity capability.
We offer a competitive salary , a flexible working environment, modern technologies and the opportunity to take real ownership of your work.
We are looking for people who ask good questions, understand complex systems and want to build security solutions that work in practice.
Sound like you? We look forward to meeting you.
